$comment: Expected destinations per scenario for the egress harness (.plan/11-verification.md). `allow` lists every destination a run may attempt; anything else fails. `require` lists destinations that must appear. Patterns match on the fields they name; `host` and `path` accept `*` globs. Layers: inference (fake model servers), proxy (recording proxy: `connect` is a CONNECT attempt, `request` a plain request), dns (Linux resolver log), sink (Linux any-IP sink), sandbox (macOS sandbox denials; the kernel masks the address but keeps port and process). These encode the acceptance contract, not the current binary, so a baseline run is expected to fail where the audit says so.

S0.description: Bypass fixture: a raw connect to 192.0.2.1:443 that ignores the proxy. The namespace layer must record it or the harness is blind: on Linux the sink sees 192.0.2.1:443, on macOS the sandbox kills the fixture.

S1.description: Local session under preset private: only the loopback provider, no DNS, nothing else.

S2.description: S1 plus one scripted webfetch to a second loopback server; the fetch is the only non-inference traffic.

S3.description: Local model drops the connection mid-stream and stays down; retries hit loopback only.

S4.description: Third-party session under preset external: only api.fireworks.ai (served by the fake TLS server through the proxy MITM route).

S5.description: Preset private with a third-party provider enabled: startup error, no requests at all.

S6.description: TUI idle: no connections of any kind.

S7.description: Title, compaction, subagent, and agent generation all go to the loopback endpoint.

S8a.description: small_model points at a third-party provider: the secondary call is rejected, the primary session continues on loopback.

S8b.description: A plugin small-model hook returns a third-party model: same expectation as S8a.

S9.description: Project opencode.json tries to raise the preset, add a remote provider, mark it user-owned, and route small_model to it: ignored, loopback only.

S10.description: Remote endpoint labelled local by config: classified USER, rejected under private, never contacted.

S11.description: Same provider ID, one model with a per-model baseURL on a second host: that model is classified on its own and rejected under private.

S12.description: Loopback server answers 307 to a second host: the request fails and the second host is never contacted.

S13.description: A Fireworks key in the isolated auth file: startup succeeds, Fireworks is never contacted.

S14a.description: TypeScript file opened with empty caches and OPENCODE_DISABLE_LSP_DOWNLOAD set: no download attempt.

S14b.description: Same without the flag: the language-server download attempt to the npm registry is expected and logged; it carries no context markers.

S15b.description: S7 (without agent generation) on the native runtime.
